#3368. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

When you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

While this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

#3367. Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure

The Signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with Edward Snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol.

In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” …

“Formal verification” is the term given to mathematically proving or disproving that a cryptographic algorithm or protocol satisfies its security claims under all conditions. It guarantees that there is no situation in which the protocol will fail. This is a far higher standard than traditional testing methods which seek to find vulnerabilities but cannot promise that others do not exist.

Using agentic AI to carry out formal verification is a huge breakthrough for cryptography and AI alike. It is, however, extremely computationally demanding, so Google told Wired it’s unclear as yet how practical it will be to use it more broadly.

DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

It’s important to note that the validation is for the protocol itself rather than the Signal app as a whole. However, encouragement can be taken from the fact that when tested against older versions of Signal that contained known vulnerabilities, it identified those and flagged them as failing formal verification.

Also worth stating is that Google was able to build on some past formal verification work already completed without the use of AI. This analysis took four weeks, and the scale of resources required has not yet been disclosed, so we shouldn’t expect a whole array of other protocols to be validated overnight. All the same, this is a very big deal.

#3366. Skip Hinnant, Peanuts Star, Dies At 86

Skip Hinnant, the beloved actor behind one of Peanuts' classic characters, has sadly passed away.

Hinnant, who played Schroeder in the Off-Broadway musical You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown and the voice behind Fritz the Cat, died on Sunday, November 8, 2026, in Denver, Colorado, according to a statement published by The New York Times. His family say that the actor was surrounded by loved ones at the time of his death. The cause of death has not been publicly disclosed at the time of this article's publication.

Hinnant was part of the original 1967 cast of the musical, You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown, portraying Schroeder in the stage play inspired by Charles M. Schulz's Peanuts comic strip. The production also featured his older brother, Bill Hinnant, who portrayed Snoopy, Gary Burghoff took on the role of the main character, Charlie Brown; and Bob Balaban played Linus.

The CMF Watch Pro is a basic smartwatch. It features 110 tracking modes, a secure fit, up to two weeks of battery life, and IP68 durability. However, there were data discrepancies and missing fitness-tracking stats, and I think the newer, cheaper CMF Watch 3 Pro is a better buy.

Can only be purchased through third-party sellers

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

For anyone starting out on a fitness journey, one of the newest and best smartwatches isn’t always essential. You can still get useful metrics by using an older model, although I’m not sure the CMF Watch Pro is the answer for everyone.

There’s a lot to like about this watch, such as the durable build quality and the excellent battery life. It tracks 110 fitness modes and has a secure strap for HIIT workouts, but when it comes to data, there’s something missing.

There were discrepancies in the fitness data compared to other fitness trackers, and there was occasional missing data when tracking sleep and overall health. The watch face was also far too large for my wrist. To find out more, keep reading this full CMF Watch Pro review.

Accelerometer, heart rate monitor, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) sensor

The CMF Watch Pro is available to purchase from the third-party retailer AliExpress in the U.S. for $123 and in the U.K. for £109. The watch is available in four colors, including Dark Grey, Ash Grey, Silver and Orange.

The watch launched in September 2023 and has previously been available for as low as $69. However, it’s no longer available for purchase from Amazon or Nothing’s website, and its price has nearly doubled, so I wouldn’t recommend purchasing it anymore.

You can get the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro for the much lower price of $79, and it has more advanced features like dual-band GPS and 131 sport modes. It also has a circular watch face, which in my opinion looks sleeker, instead of the square face of the CMF Watch Pro.

If you just want to track wellness and don’t feel you need to look at a screen for your workout stats, the Fitbit Air is a great option for $99. This screen-free device can detect and track up to 100 sports and activities, and forgoes the distraction of a screen, which I personally love.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Amazfit Bip 6 is cheaper at $79 and performs far better. Sleep tracking is more accurate on the Bip 6 in comparison to the CMF Watch Pro. The Bip 6 can also track a wider variety of workouts.

CMF by Nothing is well known for its quirky design ethos, but the CMF Watch Pro seems to be a simple ode to the Apple Watch. With a square, 1.96-inch AMOLED touch-screen display, it feels very bulky on my wrist. It’s the same size as the larger variant of the Apple Watch Series 11. However, the CMF watch is nowhere near as chunky as the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro, which takes up more real estate on my arm.

The CMF Watch Pro has an aluminum alloy frame case, and it feels very sturdy. It took a few bumps while I was carrying out my daily tasks, but there are no scratches at all. The watch is very durable, with a rating of IP68, meaning it is completely dust-tight and can be submerged underwater. I wouldn’t recommend purchasing a watch with anything less than this level of protection, as you want it to be able to carry you through every activity. With that said, it’s not the best you can get. Other watches such as the Amazfit Bip 6 have a durability rating of 5ATM which means it can withstand underwater pressure, making it far better for sports.

There is a button on the right side, which cycles through watch settings, but it’s also touchscreen. The adjustable silicone wrist strap feels secure throughout workouts and didn’t cause any irritation.

The CMF Watch Pro can track up to 110 different sports. It has basic workouts like running, walking, weight training, and Pilates.

It counts my daily steps, tracks my heart rate throughout activities, and has smart detection to automatically recognise some activities. You can also sync the data it collects with third-party apps like Strava and Apple Health, but you can’t integrate these apps into the watch.

My average heart rate after each workout I measured was around the same as my Oura Ring 5, so I’d say the watch’s tracking here is pretty accurate. However, I noticed that my peak heart rate wasn’t the same — the CMF Watch Pro logged it a lot lower— and I logged around 700 steps less than my Oura Ring and phone each day. It’s a good-enough watch if you only need the very basics, but why not just purchase something similarly-priced with a bit more accuracy? I’d recommend the Amazfit Bip 6 or the Xiaomi Smart Band 10 for monitoring during workouts with more accuracy.

Health monitoring and sleep tracking are very basic on the CMF Watch Pro, and there are some discrepancies when compared to other devices, so this probably isn’t the best option for fitness fanatics.

The CMF Watch Pro’s health tracking capabilities are basic. There’s 24-hour heart rate tracking and blood oxygen monitoring, but no ECG. If you want this you’ll have to spend more on the Apple Watch Series 11. It can also track your stress. These are important metrics if you’re managing a health condition, however there was missing data and discrepancies during activity when compared to other tracking devices. The step counts were inaccurate when compared to my Oura Ring and my peak heart rate wasn’t always captured. I also experienced this issue when using the CMF Watch 3 Pro.

You can also set up reminders on the watch for hydration and standing up. I personally like the stand-up reminder; I sometimes need a nudge to take a stretch break.

Interestingly, sleep tracking on the CMF Watch Pro is more accurate than the CMF Watch 3 Pro. The CMF Watch Pro tracked my full sleep; however, it was unbroken, whereas my Oura Ring picked up some accurate wake times.

I found the sleep analysis in the Nothing X app very basic. Since I like to track my sleep to evaluate readiness to account for my training load, having more information about movement and getting feedback on readings is often very helpful. If that’s something you want, the Xiaomi Smart Band 10 is a great option for $51.

The CMF Watch Pro gets up to 13 days of battery life per charge, but heavy use decreases this to around 11 days, which is still impressive. It took an hour to fully charge. It has the same battery life rating as the CMF Watch 3 Pro, and the more I consider the two devices, there’s not much separating them apart from their shape and an upgraded GPS system.

When the CMF Watch Pro is in power-saving mode, you can get up to 45 days of use. This obviously limits what you can do and won’t track your metrics continuously, and at that point you may as well just have an analog watch on your wrist.

The CMF Watch Pro is a solid option for anyone buying their first smartwatch. More advanced watches can seem overwhelming; this is a great entry-level option with 110 tracking modes and a secure and reliable fit. The battery can last almost two weeks, and the IP68 rating means it’s ready for anything, so you don’t need to take it off.

However, the large face of the CMF Watch Pro wasn’t the best fit for my wrist and led to some missing data and discrepancies in my fitness tracking compared to other watches. you may as well buy the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro, as there’s not that much difference between the two, and weirdly, the new watch is cheaper.

#3363. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

There’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

According to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

#3362. This Beloved Sci-Fi Novel Is Finally Getting Adapted After 12 Years, but It’s All Wrong

After 12 years and at least two scrapped attempts, Red Rising by Pierce Brown is finally getting adapted for the screen. Last month, Paramount Pictures announced that it had purchased the film rights to the acclaimed science fiction series, and it had even assigned writer Justin Rhodes and director Francis Lawrence to the project. The news broke days after Paramount's parent company finalized its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating the conglomerate now known simply as Skydance. With that much new momentum behind it, things are looking pretty good for this project, yet many fans still feel it taking the wrong approach. Like other doorstopper novels, this story might be better suited to a series than movies, and it might actually look better if it was animated rather than live-action.

These arguments have been made for several recent adaptations, and they've become increasingly popular among fans online. In this case, Brown actually spoke up about the idea of animation directly on social media. He told fans that he is simply trying to give the story its best chance at succeeding on the big screen, intimating that there are some very complex legal issues at play behind the scenes. Brown even suggested that an animated adaptation could come later if there's demand for it.

In a discussion with fans on Instagram, Brown assured fans that he did not compromise his own wishes in this latest deal to adapt Red Rising. It sounds like the author himself has wanted a live-action movie from the start. He explained: "If the film works, everything is on the table. If the film fails, animation is still on the table. If animation worked... Goddamn you don't comprehend the legal/rights complexity it'd take to make it a film. If animation failed, it's dead."

It sounds like Brown's pursuit of a live-action adaptation was at least partially motivated by the logic of sales. It's nice to see him assuring fans that he is not opposed to the idea of animation for this story. Red Rising is set in a distant future where humanity has colonized the entire solar system. It takes place on various planets, moons, and spacecraft, all with elaborate terraforming and engineering in place. On top of that, the characters are often flying, battling with advanced weaponry, or pulling off even more outrageous stunts that are hard to picture in live-action.

A "live-action" adaptation of Red Rising will really be a mass of special effects and CGI, which is why animation is such a popular option for fans. If the most important elements of the story are going to be animated by artists anyway, why not simplify the whole thing with a more stylized look? However, Brown's comments seem to suggest that it would be extremely difficult to sell a live-action adaptation after an animated adaptation, especially if the animated adaptation was unprofitable. That means the franchise's current course is its best chance of succeeding on multiple fronts, and it leaves other doors open as well.

Just a decade and a half ago, the idea of a fantasy novel adaptation performing better as a ten-episode series than a movie would have sounded strange in Hollywood, then Game of Thrones came along. Today, many other long, epic fantasy and sci-fi novels are succeeding as series, and the medium seems to suit their stories better than movies would have. It may be that in a few years, we'll look back and talk about animated adaptations in the same way.

Animation is a natural choice for many of the best sci-fi and fantasy books, especially if the adaptations are going to rely heavily on CGI. These stories could look beautiful in the hands of talented artists and animators, while voice actors could bring the characters to life. Sadly, animation is still seen as a medium for children, or for cheap, niche projects. If Hollywood can shift its attitude towards animation the way it did with TV adaptations, we could enter a whole new golden age of sci-fi and fantasy on the screen. This practice could reign in some of the unbelievable budgets monopolizing the industry and put creative control back in the hands of a small, nimble team again.

That won't be the style for this upcoming adaptation of Red Rising, but it's good to know that the option is still there. So far there's no word on when the movie will start production or when it might hit theaters. In the meantime, there are six novels in the Red Rising saga available now in print, digital, and audiobook formats. Brown has been hard at work on the seventh and final novel, and could announce its publication date any day now.

#3360. Ring’s wheeled and flying robots will patrol your home

Some people use a whole bunch of fixed cameras to monitor their homes, but Amazon has just announced a more flexible solution through wheeled and flying robots.

Both the $250 Drone Cam and $1,000 Rover Cam can respond to alarms or door and window sensor alerts in order to go check out what’s happening and send live video …

Amazon says they are the first two Ring Robotics products, with more likely to follow. Both are autonomous.

Ring Drone and Ring Rover are both powered by AI Pilot, a custom-built system that uses the devices’ cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.

AI Pilot simplifies the customer experience, starting with setup. Simply carry Ring Drone through your space or let Ring Rover autonomously explore, and it turns what it sees into a floor plan. It intelligently identifies rooms and suggests patrol points: spots worth extra attention. This could be a side door, windows, a register, or a long corridor, helping eliminate guesswork while also allowing you to add additional points customized to your space and security preferences.

When a patrol or flight is initiated, AI Pilot plans the most efficient route to get to a preset point based on the map it’s created. From there, it reacts in real time—autonomously navigating around furniture, shelving, and any obstacle it encounters.

You can set either device to patrol on a fixed schedule, as well as activate them manually, but they will also automatically respond to sensor alerts and alarms.

When a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm is triggered, [either device] automatically [moves] to previously set patrol points to investigate […] Continuous person motion detection means Ring Rover can alert you and start recording the moment it detects motion in its view—even when docked.

The Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping on December 16 for $999.99, but you can preorder it today. The Drone Cam starts shipping in late January for $249.99, but there’s no preorder yet.

#3359. Adobe unveils new AI tools for Photoshop, Premiere, and more, with MCP support coming in 2027

Adobe today announced a sweeping set of updates at its annual Adobe MAX conference, focused on giving users more ways to automate complex workflows, edit content, and work across its creative apps. Here are the details.

At the Adobe MAX event today, the company unveiled a series of features, many of them AI-powered or AI-assisted, that will begin rolling out across its suite of creative platforms as early as today.

In Photoshop, the new Relight tool offers a way to non-destructively and dynamically add, reposition, and resize light sources in the composition, while Generative Restylelets users** prompt the platform to generate variations of an image’s style and fine-tune the results using adjustable sliders.

Photoshop is also adding a Quick Compare slider to make it easier to track before-and-after results, and is getting several features in the beta app, including, per Adobe:

Following its acquisition of Topaz Labs, Adobe is also introducing two new AI image enhancement models: Wonder 4, which combines upscaling, denoising, deblurring, and sharpening into a single operation, and Image HDR, which converts standard images into HDR with improved brightness and detail.

Adobe Premiere is also getting generative tools that make it easier to prepare raw files for a project, including Enhance Audio, Separate Crosstalk, and Separate Sound Source. Adobe is also adding a Generative Remove tool to Premiere in beta, “bringing you the power to remove unwanted objects, like boom mics and logos or background distractions, directly on your timeline,” says the company.

Premiere is also getting Color Mode, a new color-grading tool starting today, which “supports everything from quick corrections to more advanced grades while keeping your video as the focus.”

Another interesting tool making its way into Premiere is Generative Media Tool. Here’s Adobe:

The Generative Media Tool brings Generate Video, Generate Sound Effects, Generate Soundscape and Generate Music directly into your timeline in Premiere. You can generate missing b-roll, background music or sound for a scene using context from your edit, then keep refining the result in your timeline. You can also choose from Adobe Firefly and models from partners including Google, Kling, Runway and Luma based on the creative needs of your project.

As for iPhone users who rely on Premiere Mobile, Adobe announced that its newly established partnerships with UMG and WMG will bring hundreds of thousands of licensed music tracks to the app (for non-commercial use) starting today, with users able to explore trending songs, discover featured artists, and create videos using artist-inspired templates.

Premiere mobile is also getting agentic tools soon, including Quick Cuts, which generates a first cut based on the user’s prompt and the materials they add, and an AI Assistant, which helps users find the right editing tools and execute tasks based on natural language instructions.

In Lightroom, the company is adding multiple new tools that make it easier to edit or more quickly fix small imperfections. That includes Glow, which “adds soft, cinematic light to your photos,” Blemish Removal for quick skin fine-tuning, Open Eyes in beta, and an improved and expanded Camera Tethering on Desktop and the iPad, with support for more cameras and advanced shooting controls, plus the ability to connect cameras directly to an iPad for live previews and photo editing.

Adobe is adding new brushes, gradients, patterns, and graphic styles to Illustrator, alongside new Blend controls, which “make it easier to develop and refine designs with a persistent control panel and live preview,” per the company.

As for InDesign, a new Co-editing feature, available in beta, streamlines collaborative work, while the new Flex Layout tool dynamically adjusts content based on the canvas size and artwork. InDesign is also getting Check Document and Rewrite that more quickly “help identify common editorial and accessibility issues while you’re still working.”

While it will not launch until 2027, this feature will enable users to connect Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects to the AI tools and agents they already use.

In practice, this will mean connecting Photoshop to ChatGPT and having them work in tandem to adapt an entire campaign based on new artwork you develop and attach to your prompt.

This integration will also account for other connected tools, so the user can ask ChatGPT to make edits, add new files to a Google Drive folder, update the team on Slack, and so on.

Here’s Adobe on the upcoming MCP integration:

Because it runs locally on your computer, your agent works directly in your native project files, and your layers, vectors, bins and sequences stay editable.

The company notes that MCP integrations will enter private beta in early 2027, and users can sign up here to learn more.

According to Adobe, Firefly is getting even better at helping users organize and edit their raw material for tasks such as turning travel clips into a vlog, creating social media campaigns, or assembling videos from storyboards.

The new Firefly Video lets users organize scenes, assemble clips, add captions, and generate transitions and B-roll, while Firefly Design brings illustration, image editing, animation, and 3D tools into a single canvas.

Adobe is also adding Quick Actions for common editing tasks, Firefly Graph for creating reusable workflows, and Firefly Builder (in private beta) for prototyping websites and apps using natural language.

Firefly’s AI Assistant is also getting new capabilities, including Plan Mode, which lets users review and approve an agent’s proposed actions, and Model Selector, which lets them choose which AI model to use.

Adobe is also previewing Always-on agents, which can handle recurring tasks such as organizing assets, checking quality, and preparing content for different platforms in the background, even when users step away.

Adobe is also expanding its Creative Agent across Creative Cloud, with AI Assistants now available in beta in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign, After Effects, and Frame.io, as well as the Photoshop beta app.

These assistants allow users to execute complex, multi-step tasks using natural language prompts. In Premiere, for example, users can ask the assistant to apply effects to an entire sequence, track subjects across frames, or adjust color and exposure across multiple clips.

To learn more about these and other features announced at Adobe MAX today, stay tuned to the company’s blog.

#3354. The 8 Greatest Vampire Books Released Since 'Dracula', Ranked

The vampire is one of the most enduring monsters in fiction, shifting in step with the times. Supernatural bloodsuckers have existed in folklore for centuries, but they took their core modern form in Bram Stoker's seminal Dracula back in 1897. Since then, countless writers have built on, tweaked, or subverted those ideas over the last 129 years.

This list looks at the finest of those books released in the wake of Dracula, from the blockbuster dark fantasy of Empire of the Vampire to the small-town horror of Salem's Lot. Some of the titles below retain the traditional Gothic atmosphere, while others incorporate sci-fi, psychological horror, historical fiction, or character study.

"Too much hate will burn a man to cinders." Empire of the Vampire is a great hybrid of vampire tropes and epic fantasy, courtesy of Jay Kristoff, author of Nevernight and The Lotus War. The story takes place in a high fantasy world decades after a mysterious catastrophe known as Daysdeath obscured the sun, allowing vampires to emerge from the shadows and conquer much of human civilization. Its protagonist, Gabriel de León, is a former member of the Silver Order, an organization of warriors trained to hunt the undead.

Imprisoned by his enemies, Gabriel recounts his extraordinary life to a vampire historian, from his upbringing and military exploits to his desperate quest to recover humanity's last hope. The atmosphere is delectably Gothic the whole way through, and elevated by intricate, lovingly crafted worldbuilding. For instance, the different vampire bloodlines all have distinct powers and belief systems.

"Do you see? I am a vampire." This book was an important milestone in the development of vampires in popular fiction, even years before the blockbuster movie adaptation. In particular, it broke ground by treating its bloodsuckers as psychologically complex protagonists capable of guilt, desire, existential despair, and perhaps even growth. The plot focuses on Louis de Pointe du Lac, a vampire who tells his life story to a young journalist in modern-day San Francisco.

Louis is a compelling protagonist. He struggles with the moral implications of his existence, repeatedly questioning whether his need to consume human blood makes him fundamentally evil. Lestat, meanwhile, embraces immortality with an enthusiasm that both fascinates and horrifies his companion. On top of that, the book throws in a powerful sensual and romantic subtext, which would greatly influence the genre going forward.

"Innocence ain't all it's cracked up to be." Layered characters and genuine horror are the name of the game here. This banger from Joe Hill (the mind behind Horns and King Sorrow) follows Victoria McQueen, a young woman who discovers that she has the power to locate lost objects by riding her bicycle across a mysterious covered bridge. This unusual talent eventually brings her into conflict with Charlie Manx, a seemingly immortal predator who abducts children and transports them to a nightmarish supernatural realm.

Manx travels in a sinister Rolls-Royce Wraith, using his vehicle to drain the life from his victims while maintaining his unnatural longevity. NOS4A2 is a fresh riff on vampire mythology. Just like traditional vampires, Manx grows decrepit and weak when he goes too long without feeding, but he consumes souls directly rather than drinking blood, and behaves more like a serial killer from a thriller than one of the alluring yet dangerous vampires of yore.

"Dusk is the time when men whisper of matters about which they remain silent in the full light of the sun." This one is a little more obscure, but it has something of a cult following. The main character is Richard Fountain, a brilliant young Cambridge scholar who travels to Greece and becomes tangled up with a mysterious, mesmerizing, dangerous woman named Chriseis. Soon, he'staking part in twisted, sadistic rituals, and his friends, growing concerned, set out in search of him.

Instead of playing that premise as pulp and relying on conventional Gothic imagery, the book distinguishes itself through its unusual combination of intellectual sophistication and provocative subject matter, especially for 1960. Doctors Wear Scarlet explores the psychological dimensions of vampirism, leaning hard into obsession, control, forbidden desires, and the darker impulses concealed beneath respectable social masks.

"The world was gone, and he was alone." This classic greatly influenced both vampire and zombie fiction. Most notably, it was the first vampire story to strip away the magic and make its bloodsuckers the result of a global pandemic, a conceit that pretty much spawned a new subgenre unto itself. At the center of the plot is survivor Robert Neville, who lives alone in a fortified house, spending his days gathering supplies, researching the disease, and hunting the infected.

At night, he barricades himself indoors while the vampires gather outside, attempting to lure him into their clutches. Much of the suspense comes from watching Neville's attempts to understand the biological mechanisms behind the creatures' behavior. In this approach, I Am Legend takes the themes of superstition-versus-science even further than Dracula originally did, culminating in a punchy, unforgettable ending that remains subversive and iconic.

"Some nights the darkness comes down so thick you can almost taste it." Set in 1857, Fevre Dream follows Abner Marsh, a struggling steamboat captain whose fortunes change when he is hired by a mysterious gentleman named Joshua York. However, Abner becomes increasingly suspicious of Joshua's peculiar habits, particularly his secretive conversations and aversion to sunlight.

Long before finding mainstream success with A Game of Thrones, George R. R. Martin penned one of the richest and most immersive vampire novels of the late 20th century. While some of the plot mechanics are familiar, the backdrop is unique: the action unfolds on boats navigating the Mississippi River in the antebellum era. That setting feels really authentic. Not to mention, Martin also hits hard with the themes. For instance, he presents philosophies concerning the relationship between humanity and its supernatural predators.

"To flee is life. To linger, death." Most readers will be familiar with the brilliant film adaptation, but many won't be aware that Let the Right One In was originally a book. Set in the Stockholm suburb of Blackeberg during the early 1980s, the novel follows Oskar, a bullied twelve-year-old boy whose miserable existence begins changing when he befriends Eli, a mysterious child who has recently moved into his apartment complex. Needless to say, she turns out to be a vampire.

In contrast to most vampire fiction in the 2000s, Let the Right One In does not romanticize the monster. Eli's existence is defined by violence and isolation, becoming a mirror to the ordinary people around her, who also struggle with addiction, exploitation, despair, and inner darkness. The relationship between Oskar and Eli forms the heart of the story, developing into a complicated friendship at once tender and deeply unsettling.

"The town knew about darkness." This book has been described as "Peyton Place meets Dracula", and that's exactly right. Stephen King's sophomore (published) novel is one of his strongest, fusing vampire mythology with realistic small-town drama. It's an ensemble piece, but the central character is Ben Mears, a novelist who returns to the town of Jerusalem's Lot, Maine, hoping to confront traumatic memories from his childhood. However, his arrival coincides with the appearance of two sinister newcomers, Richard Straker and Kurt Barlow.

Soon afterward, residents begin disappearing or exhibiting strange behavior, slowly becoming an army of the undead. Again, that could easily have become a schlocky penny dreadful, but King makes it vastly more interesting because the community feels real. He paints a sprawling, convincing portrait of ordinary people, marked by complicated relationships and private resentments. This meticulous development makes the town's gradual destruction all the more horrifying.

#3353. Apple’s new HomeView to add two major features not yet announced, per leaks

Apple’s HomeView arrives this Friday (pre-order here), but leaks indicate there are already two major new features in the works that haven’t been announced. Here’s what to expect.

It’s been a busy product launch season for Apple, and the company isn’t done quite yet.

Two new Home products arrive in stores this Friday, November 13: Apple HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K.

Yet despite the HomeView still being days away from launch, leaks in Apple code have already revealed two unannounced features that are in the works.

Leaker pdfu discovered evidence in HomeView 27.2 software that Apple is preparing for the product to add security camera functionality.

Based on pdfu’s findings, much of the work has already been done for HomeView to integrate with HomeKit Secure Video.

However, Apple hasn’t announced any sort of security camera functionality, so there’s clearly still more work to be done and it’s always possible the feature is never enabled.

Additionally, pdfu found a key change in iOS 27.3’s beta that reveals support for third-party AI apps is coming to HomeView.

HomeView has a unique third-party app story. There’s no App Store, but the product can run CarPlay-compatible apps from your iPhone automatically. At launch, only audio and video apps will be supported.

But iOS 27.3’s beta code adds “conversational apps” as a third category of supported apps. That’s what AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are classified as in CarPlay.

Nobody should buy a HomeView in the hope of these two features being added. But if you are interested in HomeView, it sounds like Apple has an ambitious set of software updates planned for its new product.

You can pre-order Apple’s HomeView here for $299.

Would either of these HomeView additions impact a purchase decision for you? Let us know in the comments.

#3352. Marvel's New Villains Are The Game-Changing Opposite Of Hydra

Warning! This post contains SPOILERS for Captain America #17

Marvel has just debuted the game-changing opposite of Hydra. Of course, Hydra has been one of the Marvel Universe's most enduring villain organizations and a classic foe of Captain America. However, it looks as though Steve Rogers will soon be facing an all-new threat, one that hits much closer to home in the pages of Marvel Comics.

In the past, Hydra's primary mission has been global dominance in a bid to assert its fascist ideals and order across the entire globe. They've existed for millennia, a cabal that refuses to die even in the Marvel Universe's modern era. However, a brand-new villain organization has just been revealed in the pages of the new Captain America #17 by writer Chip Zdarsky with art by Ton Lima.

Having already kidnapped a major Avenger with teases about their dark leader, here's everything we know about Marvel's new villain group known as the Knomads, and how they differ from Hydra.

As seen in Captain America #17, the Knomads' debut quickly establishes them as a significant threat with the reveal that they've kidnapped Tony Stark's Iron Man, explaining why Steve Rogers has been unable to contact his fellow Avenger. Its members are shown wearing simple white masks, with one of the Knomads claiming that people like Stark are a symptom of a dying United States. They then threaten to "drag his corpse through the streets of the country he's fed off for far too long" if Iron Man doesn't provide the intel they're after.

Combined with some synopses and promotional material, it seems the Knomads are motivated by an American nationalist agenda to "make their country great again", as opposed to Hydra's wider goals of full worldwide supremacy.

While both factions seem to share a focus on imposing their respective versions of order, the Knomads are specifically focused on one nation in particular (their own). Likewise, kidnapping an Avenger as powerful and influential as Tony Stark indicates that they're well organized and have major plans to enforce their vision beyond just being a fringe political movement. This is likely thanks to the man who's already been teased as their dark leader in the Marvel Universe: Grant Rogers.

The Knomads' introduction goes hand in hand with the ending twist in Captain America #17, with the reveal that it is not Steve Rogers on the run and protecting the young clone of Victor von Doom, but Grant Rogers, the former Hydra Captain America from Marvel's Secret Empire storyline. While he had most recently been a Flag-Smasher, it seems Grant has started impersonating Steve once again, having taken Steve's shield and sharing his twisted takes on American values with Vic throughout, likely in a bid to corrupt and shape the young clone into a Doctor Doom for America.

#3351. The Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is just $229, the cheapest bean-to-cup espresso machine I’ve ever seen; unfortunately, it looks and acts like it too — no Breville-beater

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

At just $229, the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is the cheapest bean-to-cup I’ve ever seen. It even has a PID controller, built-in timer, and a nice, weighty tamper. Surely this is too good to be true? Well, if you’re a coffee nerd, yes. The grinder is really inconsistent and the steam wand is quite weak — not to mention the pressurized-only portafilters. Could that sweet, sweet price of $229 be enough to convince you, though? I’m not sure it convinced me.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

When I saw the price of the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder, my eyes bulged out of my head like a cartoon rabbit being chased by a mountain lion. $229? For an espresso machine… and a grinder? What year is this, 2001?

It’s hard to explain just how cheap $229 is, but I’ll do my best. The entry-level Casabrews Tornado grinder is $139 — and that’s seriously budget. The De’Longhi Stilosa espresso machine is $149 — and, again, that’s seriously budget. So $229 for a grinder and an espresso machine is literally unheard of.

So, how does the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder hold up? Well, it’s $229. That’s all I really have to say. While, yes, this is the cheapest bean-to-cup I’ve ever seen, it performs like it. But this might be enough to make it one of your best espresso machines if you’re on a budget best described as “as close to zero as possible”. Find out the full story in this Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder review.

2 x pressurized portafilters, scoop, tamper, tamping collar, brush

The Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is $229 from Amazon U.S. and £239 from Amazon U.K. On Amzchef’s website, the Espresso Machine with Grinder is listed as “All-in-One” espresso machine and is $299 rather than $229. The “Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder” is a completely different product with a different screen style — albeit $229, not $299. I've raised this with Amzchef and have been informed it will correct this inconsistency.

They don’t make it easy for us, huh? Anyway, I would buy from Amazon due to the lower price. For ease of searching, the product code is CM1626 — but Amzchef doesn’t list this on its website (for any of its products… just a wonderful, transparent business strategy, I know). The links above are to the Amazon page, not Amzchef’s site.

Opaque pricing aside, the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is incredibly cheap. As I wrote in my “Pros” section above, it’s almost unbelievably cheap. A bean-to-cup espresso machine for $229? Seriously? Most electric grinders start at $150, like the Casabrews Tornado or Breville Dose Control Pro.

The only machines I’ve tested around the same price are the $350 Gevi Espresso Machine with Grinder and the $350 Casabrews Marenza. While this machine is a seriously budget option, the low, low pricing does raise questions about longevity — which I’ll get into later.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is a cheap coffee machine, and it feels like it. The scoop is flimsy plastic, and the dosing collar isn’t wide enough to allow the tamper to pass through. The tamper itself is lovely and weighty, though.

There’s no milk jug, which isn’t unprecedented, but is still a kick in the teeth. Casabrews also ships its budget machines with no milk jug, but it sells one for $10. Amzchef doesn’t sell a milk jug at all, so you’ll have to buy a separate one from another brand.

On top of that, the steam wand is supposed to have a 360° swivel, but I’d describe it more as 200° grating. Every time I moved the steam wand, the metal grated against the ball joint.

There’s a bright screen with full-color pictures, which also houses the built-in timer and temperature adjustment screen. This screen is the best part of the machine’s design, although I’m not sure it’s enough of a unique selling point to recommend buying it.

Considering the Amzchef Espresso Machine has a built-in grinder, I was extremely concerned when I unboxed two pressurized portafilter baskets. If you don’t know the difference between pressurized and non-pressurized baskets, I’ll give you a quick rundown. Pressurized portafilter baskets use two walls to force the espresso through a little hole, which creates fluffier crema but destroys delicate flavors. You should use pressurized portafilter baskets if you have pre-ground coffee or an inferior grinder (subtle foreshadowing).

Non-pressurized portafilter baskets have a mesh-like bottom, which allows the espresso to extract naturally, with no extra pressure — that all comes from the fineness of the grind. These baskets are a little trickier to use for beginners, but brew delicate, nuanced espresso if you have a good grinder and good beans.

So I was immediately suspicious when I saw the pressurized baskets. If I’m using a machine with a built-in grinder — ergo, freshly ground coffee — surely I should be provided non-pressurized baskets? A dual-walled basket will over-pressurize my espresso and mask delicate flavors.

Anyway, I had to use what Amzchef provided, so I, of course, tested it with said pressurized baskets.

By default, the grinder grinds for 7 seconds. This resulted in 17.3g of coffee during my tests, but obviously this will change if you grind finer or coarser for different beans. I set the grinder to click 5, as this pulled the ideal 1:2 ratio in 25-28 seconds.

Then, the machine automatically doses water. It pulled 35g of coffee in 28 seconds, which is almost the perfect 1:2 ratio in 25-28 seconds.

Here’s a photo of said default shot. This is with zero customizations — straight from the machine’s brain.

The crema is a little flat, and there’s not a whole lot of depth to the shot. I usually love watching the black ‘body’ of the shot rise up after extraction, but that wasn’t the case with this espresso. It brewed this dark amber color and this dark amber color it remained. As for the taste, it was a little bitter, not particularly strong or weak, but it got the job done. If you’re a total beginner, this would be good enough, but coffee enthusiasts would be better off elsewhere.

However, coffee enthusiasts might be the intended target audience here. There are a few premium, coffee snob-certified features on the Amzchef. You’ve got a PID controller, which controls water temperature, and you can customize temps to your liking. It can go from 190°-201°F, more versatile than Breville’s set-at-200°F PID controller, which you’d find on the $299 Breville Bambino or the $499 Breville Bambino Plus.

All of these features are excellent — I wouldn’t buy an espresso machine without — and resulted in decent espresso. Pressurized portafilters aside, this coffee sits firmly in the “good enough” category. Especially for $229, which is crazy cheap.

I have never seen a bean-to-cup semi-automatic espresso machine cheaper than the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder. I’ve tested $350 models — the aforementioned Casabrews Marenza and Gevi Espresso Machine with Grinder — but $229? That’s crazy cheap.

The grinder itself has 44 settings, so you can grind from superfine to cold-brew-coarse. As mentioned earlier, the grinder grinds for 7 seconds by default, which you can adjust. To test uniformity, I used my Kruve Coffee Sieves ($189). As espresso grounds should be 300-400 microns, I sift ground coffee through the 500-micron sieve. I’m looking for 100% pass-through. I used click 5 to test espresso, which extracted a 1:2 ratio in 28 seconds.

Here’s a photo to exemplify what I mean. The left is coffee bigger than 500 microns, and the right is coffee smaller than 500 microns (espresso size).

As you can see, this is a non-uniform, inconsistent grinder… and now I know why Amzchef only provides you dual-walled portafilters.

The steam wand is one of the biggest let-dows of the whole machine. It’s weak, spluttery, and takes over sixty seconds to steam a jug of milk (for one coffee).

To activate the steam wand itself, you have to press the steam graphic on the screen, not twist the knob on the side. After pressing the graphic, and the machine reading 107 (temperature), then you twist the knob. It needs a few seconds to switch to steam.

However, the steam wand is really disappointing. I still managed to get half-decent latte art, but the actual texture of the milk was undesirable. It had a layer of foam on top and then wet milk — no velvety aeration throughout.

As you can see, the latte art is still good. But this is after years of practice. I don’t think this is a good machine for beginners to learn on, because you have to know how to tease out “good” milk texture from a sub-par wand.

I don’t really have anything positive to say about the steam wand. If you aren’t fussed about milk drinks, this might be something you can overlook, but for me, I live for decadent, velvety milk, so it’d be a pass.

As it’s just 13 inches wide and 13 inches deep, the Amzchef Espresso Machine is relatively compact, especially for a bean-to-cup machine. If you’re seriously short on space (and budget), I might recommend the Amzchef, but that’s a might.

The machine has an “aluminum alloy” boiler, which means it’s more susceptible to corrosion than a stainless steel boiler, however, there’s no water filter slot in the water tank. Either the machine won’t last as long as a stainless steel boiler, or you’ll need to be seriously on top of descaling — even if you live in a soft water area. There are also no cleaning discs or a cleaning portafilter basket cover for backflushing, unlike Breville and De’Longhi’s machines.

Amzchef advertizes a 2-year warranty if you purchase from the Amzchef website, but the espresso machine is $70 more expensive on the Amzchef site (at time of writing — Amzchef has told me it will correct this). If you register it, the warranty increases to three years. However, you have to spend an extra $70 buying it directly from Amzchef. On the Amzchef warranty page, it reads, “Buy from Amazon, Walmart, or other online retailers? You may get an up-to-2-year limited warranty.” Schrödinger’s warranty!

Amzchef’s representative confirmed that you receive a 2-year warranty regardless of retailer, which is great news, but the language is still too opaque. What if you didn’t have a direct link to the company to find out this information (as I assume most of you won’t)? The language needs to be clearer.

Opaque business practices like this make me incredibly wary about recommending a product. It’s disingenuous. I wouldn’t spend my hard-earned money at a company with obfuscated warranty rules.

Everything about the Amzchef Espresso Machine feels too good to be true. A PID controller, customizable brew temperature, built-in grinder, cold brew, and 360° swivel steam wand for $229? There’s something not quite right here — and you can feel it in the build quality. The water tank is flimsy, the grinder hopper is flimsy, the portafilter is flimsy, and the steam wand grates as it moves. Not only that, but the steam wand is relatively weak, and the low-quality grinder makes for mediocre espresso.

This is a tricky one, because $229 is incredibly cheap for an espresso machine with a grinder. Normally, you’d be expecting to pay $229 for the espresso machine alone and an extra $229 for the grinder — and that would be cheap.

However, I can’t recommend this machine due to its low-quality build, low-quality accessories, and low-quality grinder. I would recommend grabbing the $350 Casabrews Marenza instead (but that’s also incredibly flimsy), or save up more for the Breville Barista Express — often around $499 during sales events like Black Friday — or the De’Longhi Arte Evo — also around $450 during sales events.

#3350. Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

Last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my issues, the new device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it. They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo.The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

Now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that said, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the new 10-inch model offers some big upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:

Resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side.)

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

It's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than Aura's most popular offering, the 10.1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

I write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

#3348. ‘Tracker’ Meets ‘Reacher’ in Mark Wahlberg’s Action Hit That Is Officially Removed From Free Streaming

He has covered everything from Marvel to the Oscars, and Marvel at the Oscars. He also writes obsessively about the box office, charting the many hits and misses that are released weekly, and how their commercial performance shapes public perception. In his time at Collider, he has also helped drive diversity by writing stories about the multiple Indian film industries, with a goal of introducing audiences to a whole new world of cinema.

One of the biggest sleeper hits on the PVOD market this year is a nondescript action-thriller that will turn 20 years old in a few months. The movie wasn't exactly a major hit in its theatrical run, but it has had a robust life on home video. It inspired a television spin-off, and now seems to be attracting the same audience that tunes into shows such as Tracker and Reacher. The film in question is currently streaming on Paramount+ in the United States, where, according to FlixPatrol, it has spent nearly 90 days in the top 10 this year. The movie is also available on Tubi, but only for a little while longer.

The last decade has seen a revival of procedural content, both on linear television and streaming. Shows such as Yellowstone, Bosch, and The Lincoln Lawyer have found a sweet spot between old-fashioned episodic television on TV and the cinematic scope of streaming content. Unsurprisingly, this has led to a renaissance for films like the 2007 action-thriller, likely because those who tune into these shows are promptly pointed toward similar programming on the same platforms.

This is one of the reasons for the success of movies such as The Contractor, starring Chris Pine, and the continued interest in John Krasinski's Jack Ryan franchise. The 2007 action-thriller falls squarely in the same category, and is headlined by arguably the most high-profile star to make streaming his primary home. We're talking, of course, about Mark Wahlberg, who has starred in more than half a dozen streaming originals in the last decade or so, after experiencing enormous success as a big-screen movie star.

The movie is Shooter, directed by Antoine Fuqua. Shooter is based on a novel that follows a military sniper who is framed for a crime he didn't commit; the sniper is taken in by a kind woman while he's on the run from the government. Shooter grossed $95 million at the worldwide box office, against a reported budget of $65 million. While this is a much smaller haul than Fuqua's other action hits — The Equalizer, Olympus Has Fallen, and Training Day — the film ultimately found its audience at home.

This is reflected in the film's 80% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, which it continues to hold despite a 50% critics' score. The aggregator website's consensus reads, "With an implausible story and numerous plot holes, Shooter fails to distinguish itself from other mindless action-thrillers." Shooter inspired a television reboot starring Ryan Phillippe, which ran for three seasons on the USA Network. You can watch the movie for free on Tubi until December 1.

Shooter follows a highly skilled marksman who is coaxed out of retirement for a mission to thwart an assassination plot against the President. However, he finds himself framed for the attempt, prompting a perilous journey to clear his name while uncovering a deeper conspiracy.

#3347. Apple TV launches new sign language accessibility feature

Apple today launched a neat new accessibility feature for the Apple TV streaming service. Users will now have the option to watch with a sign language interpretation for some of Apple’s original movies.

The feature is launching this Friday with the debut of the new film Being Heumann, as well as F1: The Movie. Support for more titles will follow later.

Alongside those two films, Apple said that sign language options will be available for Greyhound and Way of the Warrior Kid later this year, with more to come.

To access the new functionality, you need to be using the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad or Mac running 27.2 or later. The feature will also be available on some versions of the Apple TV app on other platforms.

By default, the Sign Language controls are hidden. If you want to use the feature, firstly go to the Settings app -> TV app, and enable the Sign Language display.

Then, on eligible titles, a new Sign Language button will appear in the player controls. You can simply toggle to enable, and choose from American Sign Language or British Sign Language modes.

When enabled, a signing interpreter then appears in the corner of the frame, synced with the video playback.

When browsing the catalog, sign language availability will also be shown next to the usual subtitle and audio language information. Users will also be able to search “with ASL” or “with BSL” to find compatible titles.

#3345. Grey's Anatomy: Why TR Knight's George O'Malley Was Killed Off In Season 6

The George O’Malley death in Grey's Anatomy season 6 and T.R. Knight's departure from the show were shocking — so how did George O'Malley die, and why was he killed off in the first place? The series is led by Meredith Grey, who started her journey as an intern along with many other characters that won the audience over before Grey's Anatomy killed them off. One of those Grey's Anatomy characters was George O’Malley (T.R. Knight), who struggled a bit but became a very skilled and talented surgeon, and the best friend of Izzie Stevens. George dies in Grey's Anatomy in season 6 due to complications from an accident.

Just when George seemed to have found his path in medicine, he planned to leave Seattle Grace in season 5 to join the U.S. Army in Iraq. But on his way home, he jumped in front of a bus to save a woman’s life and was left severely disfigured. None of Grey’s Anatomy’s doctors recognized George, and it wasn’t until he traced “007” on Meredith’s hand that they knew who the “John Doe” patient was. His brain fatally swelled during surgery. The George O’Malley death in Grey's Anatomy was a tragic ending that saw T.R. Knight leave the series in season 6 without much understanding as of why.

George left Grey's Anatomy due to some behind-the-scenes creative differences. Knight’s Grey’s Anatomy season 6 departure was announced in June 2009, and he revealed (via EW) not long after that the reason behind it was a gradual “breakdown of communication” between him and Rhimes, who he also said tried to discourage him from coming out. This led him not to ask what was going on with Grey's Anatomy's George O’Malley storylines anymore, and he simply asked to be released from his contract, leading to the George O'Malley death.

In addition, Knight wasn’t comfortable with where his character was being led to before his Grey's Anatomy season 6 (the same season when Katherine Heigl left) death and struggled with the storyline where George cheated on his wife, Callie Torres (Sara Ramirez), with Izzie. So, they killed George O'Malley to come up with a proper reason for T.R. Knight to leave the show. Knight later said he was at peace with his decision to leave Grey’s Anatomy in season 6 and end his time with the George O'Malley death scene, saying there “comes a time when it’s so clear that moving on is the best decision.”

He may have fallen prey to Grey’s Anatomy's shortfall in handling character exits, with their go-to solution being to kill them off. However, Grey’s Anatomy's George O’Malley death stands out for how abrupt and cruel it was. George dies in season 6 of Grey's Anatomy, and while it brought a lot of drama to the series, it was also a reflection of all the behind-the-scenes issues around the character, and how his ending was handled didn’t do justice to him.

While T.R. Knight found solace after the show in George O'Malley's death and his decision to exit Grey’s Anatomy in season 6, the actor and character have since returned to the series. In Grey’s Anatomy season 15, George O’Malley made a posthumous return in the episode “Flowers Grow Out of My Grave,” briefly appearing as a ghost who visits Meredith Grey on the Day of the Dead. However, this was accomplished through archived footage.

T.R. Knight later reprised his Grey’s Anatomy role in season 17, appearing in one of Meredith’s unconscious beach visions while suffering from COVID-19, in which they reflect on George O’Malley’s season 6 death. Several figures from Meredith's past visited her while on the beach, all people who were incredibly important to her, like her sister and her husband as well.

People were happy yet incredibly surprised to see T.R. Knight's George O’Malley return in a season 17 episode of Grey's Anatomy. While his reappearance was welcomed with open arms, it was difficult to imagine that the star would return given his reasoning for exiting the show and Isaiah Washington's homophobic comments towards the actor. Despite the George O'Malley death scene, he did come back in Grey's Anatomy, this time as a product of Meredith's mind. The purpose of George's reappearance on the show came down to one thing for showrunner Krista Vernoff: closure.

The George O'Malley death in season 6 was a shock to many, and some felt that the character was wronged for it. Bringing George back on Grey's Anatomy was meant to act as closure for people who thought that the character wasn't given a fair shot. Knight was originally a bit dubious when Vernoff approached him with the idea of returning to the program. However, his husband, Patrick Leahy, convinced him to return as George O’Malley. In an interview (via Deadline), Knight is able to look back fondly at the experience, recounting, "It was incredible, it was just an overwhelming feeling of love in that moment."

After the George O'Malley death in Grey's Anatomy, T.R. Knight has been in numerous movies and television programs. In 2013 he appeared in the movie 42 as Harold Parrot, and in 2015 he was in the feature film A Year and Change as Kenny. His last movie was in 2017, called Hello Again, where he played Carl. He's also appeared in numerous television programs, such as The Good Wife, the Will and Grace reboot, and Law & Order: SVU, but his most famous property is being cast in The Flight Attendant as Davey Bowden.

The George O'Malley death on Grey's Anatomy was one of the saddest moments of the show, but T.R. Knight had such an impact as the character that he was the first person that showrunner Krista Vernoff thought of to visit Meredith in her dreams as she battled with COVID-19. The thought of Meredith and George walking on the beach together through troubling times warmed her heart (via E! News). Vernoff said:

Right now in our lives, in this pandemic, pure joy is rare, and so I'm so grateful to T.R. for coming and playing, and offering that to everyone, because I think it's meaningful.

T.R. Knight essentially echoed these sentiments in an Instagram post shortly after the fated Grey's Anatomy episode. Knight mentioned how much he enjoyed working with the fellow Grey's Anatomy cast. He stated that George would "always claim [his] heart," proving that there's still a ton of love there, despite the Goerge O'Malley death. He also said that while Meredith and George love each other, it doesn't hold a candle to the love he has for Pompeo. Knight had nothing but thanks for the cast, saying, "Thank you to Ellen, Chandra, Jim, Krista, and all the familiar faces for once again sharing your beautiful light."

George wasn’t the first major death in the show. Instead, that honor went to Denny, the patient Izzy had fallen in love with. Denny, however, was a recurring character, not a member of the main cast. His death had also been telegraphed from his introduction on the show, unlike George, whose death blindsided fans since they didn’t even initially know the man hit by the bus was George.

George’s death made it clear that writing a character out of the show didn’t just mean doctors leaving for other jobs or taking a trip that never ended. A character leaving the show could truly be permanent. Killing them off became the easiest way for Grey’s Anatomy to do that once George became the first main character to get that final farewell.

If the show hadn’t killed George off, it’s entirely possible the series wouldn’t have such a brutal track record for character exits today. Fans often worry their favorite character is going to be killed when they find out an actor is leaving the show now. Beyond the audience realizing that no character is safe and that there are genuine stakes in the dramatic storylines, George’s death also had an impact because so many of the main characters had a strong connection to him and the show allowed each of them to grieve in different ways.

Izzie and Meredith were his best friends and had past romantic relationships with him. While Izzie’s grief came in waves, Meredith tried to avoid it completely. Bailey claimed him as her favorite intern and named her child after him, and following his death, she became a bit harder on those around her, putting up a wall again. Though Callie and George had divorced, they were still close. She nearly immediately broke down at the news. They were all given a spotlight without Grey’s Anatomy having to center the show on George after he was gone.

The show made a smart decision in having several weeks take place in a single episode. It allowed the characters space to mourn without requiring them to grieve for the entire next season. While some fans might have found it rushed, it worked for the show because the compressed timeline made it clear that despite this tragic event, life continued, and Grey’s Anatomy had more stories to tell.

Created by Shonda Rhimes, long-running medical drama Grey's Anatomy depicts the professional and personal lives of the employees of a Seattle hospital.

#3344. iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on

iPadOS 27.3 is currently available in beta, and it introduces a new iPad setting for app windowing that I instantly turned on. Here are the details.

I use the iPad Pro as my primary computer, and for the most part have found Apple’s software changes in iPadOS 26 and 27 to be great upgrades.

But with the powerful new windowing capabilities, there have definitely been some quirks that need refining. One of them involves resizing windows with the traffic light controls in the top-left corner.

For example, in iPadOS 27 the controls move locations and even disappear depending on the size of the window. It can be pretty frustrating.

I need to just get better about learning keyboard shortcuts for window controls. But in the meantime, iPadOS 27.3 adds a new optional setting that I instantly turned on and have been loving.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if you have ‘Windowed Apps’ enabled you’ll see a new option below it: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom’

If you use your iPad mostly with touch input, or simply haven’t used keyboard shortcuts enough to remember them, this new setting is a great way to quickly resize windows.

When the setting is enabled, two taps (or a double-click with the trackpad) will zoom the window to take up the full screen. Then you can double-tap again to revert it to its previous size.

I generally keep my app windows in specific size setups, but regularly find myself wanting to go fullscreen temporarily. The new setting provides a convenient way to do that quickly without needing the traffic light controls or my keyboard, and is a welcome refinement to iPadOS windowing.

Will you enable this new iPadOS 27.3 setting? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
